title: Given the roots of two binary trees root and subRoot, return true if there is a subtree of root with the same structure and values as subRoot.
shortTitle: Subtree of Another Tree: recursive comparison at every node
keyPoints: The solution composes two ideas: traversing the main tree and running a same-tree check at each node
The outer traversal picks candidate anchor points; the inner check verifies an exact match in structure and values
The naive approach is O(n * m) because each of n main-tree nodes may trigger a comparison scanning m candidate nodes
The efficient alternative serializes both trees with null markers and uses linear-time substring matching like KMP
The inner same-tree check must be strict: both null is match, one null is mismatch, values must equal, both subtrees must match
Delimiters and null sentinels are essential in the serialization approach to prevent false prefix matches

s1_definition.oneliner: At every node of the big tree, run a full same-tree check against the candidate; if any check passes, it is a subtree.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Subtree check** – determines whether a smaller tree appears exactly inside a larger tree with the same structure and values.
- **Outer traversal** – visits each node of the main tree as a candidate anchor point.
- **Inner check** – the standard same-tree comparison: both null is a match, one null is a mismatch, values must be equal, and both subtrees must recursively match.
- **Complexity** – O(n * m) for the naive approach; O(n + m) using serialization with linear-time substring matching.
- **Serialization** – encode both trees with explicit null markers and delimiters, then check substring containment.
s1_definition.analogy: Rajesh has the full National Bank of India org chart and a small team chart representing a known fraudulent approval pattern. He walks the big chart, and at every manager he checks whether the team hanging below matches the small chart exactly in shape and roles. If he finds one spot that matches completely, the pattern exists in the org.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Subtree Check: Outer Traversal + Inner Same-Tree

  Main Tree:        Candidate:
       CEO            VP1
      /   \          /   \
    VP1   VP2       D1   D2
   /  \     \
  D1  D2    D3

  Step 1: isSameTree(CEO, VP1)?  CEO != VP1 → false
  Step 2: recurse left → isSameTree(VP1, VP1)?
          VP1 == VP1, left D1 == D1, right D2 == D2 → true!
  Found subtree at VP1.
```

```text
  Serialization Approach

  Main: ",CEO,VP1,D1,#,#,D2,#,#,VP2,#,D3,#,#"
  Sub:  ",VP1,D1,#,#,D2,#,#"

  Check: is Sub a substring of Main? → Yes!
  (KMP gives O(n + m) time)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Subtree of Another Tree composes two ideas: traversing the main tree to pick candidate anchor points, and running a strict same-tree comparison at each anchor. The outer traversal visits every node, and at each one the inner check verifies whether the subtree rooted there is exactly identical to the candidate in both structure and values.

The naive complexity is O(n * m) because each main-tree node may trigger a full comparison. The efficient alternative serializes both trees with explicit null markers and delimiters, then checks substring containment using a linear-time matcher. The serialization must use delimiters between values and explicit null sentinels so that different tree structures are distinguishable and adjacent values cannot be confused.

The inner same-tree check must be strict: both null is a match, exactly one null is a mismatch, and values must be equal at every position. A near-match is not a subtree.

In our banking system at National Bank of India, compliance maintains templates of known fraudulent approval patterns as small trees. The detector searches for each pattern inside every branch's org hierarchy. The match must be exact in both shape and role at each position, and when branches are large with many patterns, the serialization approach provides the linear performance needed for production throughput.

Remember one sentence: traverse the main tree, run a strict same-tree check at each node, and if any check passes the candidate is a subtree.
